questions: Can you move my domain over?
Yes. Type in the domain you already have. With supported domain companies it connects in one click, and email can come from it too.

Yes. You can take card payment when someone books, so a no-show doesn't cost you the slot.

Yes. AnyPress works with HighLevel, so the people who book or write in can land in your HighLevel contacts too.

problems.body: You may be the best in town, but if no one knows it, you don't get the business.

problems.title: Customer details live on scraps of paper
problems.body: Names and numbers are in your phone, your truck and a notebook, so nobody hears from you again.

problems.title: Your community lives elsewhere
problems.body: Lessons in one app, discussions in another, payments in a third, and none of it on your domain.

problems.body: Many charge a monthly fee and a slice of every course you sell, or a price per student.

problems.title: Your students belong to the platform

problems.title: Dues by spreadsheet
problems.body: Renewals, reminders and who has paid are tracked by hand, every year.

problems.title: Events in another app
problems.body: Tickets and sign-ups live somewhere different from your website, with another bill.

problems.title: Members have nowhere to meet
problems.body: News goes out by email blast and the members' directory is a PDF that's out of date.

problems.title: Giving through a separate app
problems.body: Online giving lives in one tool, with its own fees, and the website somewhere else.

problems.title: Sign-ups on paper and in group chats
problems.body: Events and volunteer rotas are spread over sheets, texts and chats that newcomers never see.

problems.title: One volunteer knows how it works
problems.body: The site was set up by someone who has moved on, and now no one wants to touch it.

problems.title: Every location does its own thing
problems.body: Different builders, different looks and different logins make the brand hard to keep consistent.

problems.title: Every change goes through head office
problems.body: When one central site holds every location, a new opening time or local offer waits in someone's inbox.

problems.title: Each new location adds a full bill
problems.body: Every location pays full price for its own website, so growing costs the same per site forever.

problem: A different tool for every job

fix: One site does it all

fix: A help desk built in

problem: Growing means moving

Switch on parts as you need them and move up a size any time. Your site stays where it is.

questions: Why not buy two smaller plans?
Everything puts all the tools on one site, so a customer who buys, books and joins is one person, not three. It also costs less than the four other plans together, and adds a help desk.
Do I have to use every part?
No. Switch on what you need today. The rest is ready when you are.
Which size should I pick?
Small suits most new sites. Busy shops and big communities usually move to Medium or Large, and you can change any time.
Is it harder to look after?
No. We apply security fixes to every part and save it every night, the same as any other AnyPress site.

GUIDES.title: Moving your shop: a step-by-step checklist

sections.heading: Before you start
checks: Export your products (names, prices, descriptions, photos) from your current shop
Export your customer list, and note who agreed to get emails
Write down every page address that gets visits, so none of them break
List your active subscriptions and when they renew
Pick a quiet week. Avoid a sale or a launch

sections.heading: Build the new shop next to the old one
steps: Start your new shop on its free address. Your old shop keeps running.
Add your products and photos, then check prices, shipping and taxes.
Connect your payment account and place a test order.
Copy your About, Contact, Shipping and Refund pages.
Import your customer list with each person's email consent as it was.

sections.heading: Switch over
steps: Point your domain at the new shop. Visitors arrive there from that moment.
Send old page addresses to their new pages, so links and Google results keep working.
Tell your customers by email, and update the link in your social profiles.
Keep the old shop open (not selling) for a month in case you need anything from it.

sections.heading: Subscriptions
sections.body: Existing subscribers usually have to sign up again on the new shop, because card details can't be copied from one payment setup to another. Give them a simple link and a reason to do it, like a first month at a lower price.

GUIDES.title: Local trades website checklist

A few photos of real jobs, with a line on what you did and where

sections.heading: Make it easy to book
steps: Put a Book a time button at the top of every page.
List the jobs people can book online and how long each takes.
Take a deposit for longer jobs, so a no-show doesn't cost you the slot.
Turn on reminder emails the day before.

sections.heading: Look like a real business
checks: Email from your own domain, not a free address
Your licence and insurance details where customers can see them
Clear prices or a starting price for common jobs

sections.heading: Keep customers coming back
sections.body: Every booking adds the customer to your list. A short email after the job, and a seasonal reminder (like a furnace check before winter), brings repeat work without a single phone call.

sections.heading: On every product page

sections.heading: Pages your store needs

Where you ship, and where you don't

Members buy from your shop. We build and look after each site.

As income: add a monthly margin on each site to fund your programs

sections.heading: Your first month
steps: Pick three members who need a website and offer them a first-month discount.
Mention it in your newsletter and at your next event.
Ask those first members if you can show their sites to others.

sections.heading: The plan

sections.heading: What it costs

Each location buys its own site from head office's shop

PRIVACY.html:
This policy explains how Otaku Financial Management LLC, operating as Otaku Solutions ("AnyPress", "we", "us"), 2019 Robinson St, Redondo Beach, CA 90278, handles personal data. It covers anypress.io, shop.anypress.io, app.anypress.io, the AnyPress API, and the WordPress websites we host for our customers (their "Sites").

1. Two roles: our data and your Sites' data

  • Our own customers' data. When you visit our sites, buy a plan or use our dashboard or API, we decide how your data is used. For this data, we are the controller.
  • Your Sites' visitors and customers. The people who visit, buy from, join or subscribe to a Site you run with us are your visitors. You decide what data your Site collects and why, so you are the controller and AnyPress is your processor. We handle that data only to host, back up, secure and support your Site, and only on your instructions. You are responsible for your own privacy notice, consents and cookie banner on your Site, and for answering your visitors' requests. If one of your visitors contacts us, we will pass the request to you.

If you need a Data Processing Agreement (for example under GDPR), email support@anypress.io and we will provide one.

2. What we collect

When you buy a plan or use your account (shop.anypress.io):

  • name, email address, and billing address;
  • your account login (email or username and a hashed password);
  • what you bought: plans, sizes, email packs, order and subscription history, Site names and domains;
  • payment details: these go to Stripe. We see the card brand, last four digits and expiry, never the full card number;
  • messages you send us, such as support emails.

When you use the dashboard or API (app.anypress.io):

  • your sign-in details and the API keys issued to you;
  • a log of each API call and dashboard change: who made it, what was called, the result, the time, IP address and browser user agent. It does not include the content you send.

About your Sites (for running the service):

  • each Site's name, domains, size, and usage (storage used and emails sent each month);
  • the email addresses your Site sends from, and counts of emails sent.

Automatically, when you visit our sites:

  • standard server and security logs (IP address, browser, pages requested, time).
  • We do not use analytics or advertising pixels on anypress.io or the shop. If we add any, we will update this policy first.

3. How we use it

  • to create and run your Sites, and process your payments, renewals and refunds (to perform our contract with you);
  • to send receipts and important service emails, such as billing problems, usage warnings and notices that a Site is going offline;
  • to provide support;
  • to keep the service secure, prevent fraud and abuse, and enforce our Terms (our legitimate interests);
  • to keep records required by tax and accounting law (legal obligation);
  • to send marketing emails, only if you agreed, and you can unsubscribe at any time.

We do not sell your personal data, and we do not share it for cross-context behavioural advertising.

4. Sub-processors

We use these providers to run AnyPress. Each only gets the data it needs for its job.

Provider What it does for us Data involved
Stripe Payment processing for plans and email packs Billing details, payment card data, transactions
Hostinger Virtual private servers in the United States that run the shop, our API and customer Sites All data stored on the shop and on Sites

toSend Sending email: receipts from the shop (no-reply@anypress.io) and outgoing email from customer Sites Recipient addresses and email content
Vercel Hosting for anypress.io and the app.anypress.io dashboard Visitor IP addresses and requests; dashboard sessions

The shop runs on WordPress with FluentCart (checkout and subscriptions) and FluentCRM (customer email), which we host ourselves on the servers above; they don't send your data to another company. We will update this list when we add or change providers. We will add any new provider to this list before it handles your data.

5. Where your data is stored

Our servers are in the United States. Some providers (such as Cloudflare, Stripe, toSend and Vercel) may process data in other countries. If you are outside the US, your data is transferred to the US. Where the law requires it, we rely on safeguards such as the providers' Standard Contractual Clauses.

6. Cookies

We use a small number of cookies:

  • Essential cookies on shop.anypress.io keep you signed in and keep your cart and checkout working.
  • Sign-in cookies on app.anypress.io keep you signed in to the dashboard.
  • Stripe may set cookies during checkout to prevent fraud.

These are needed for the service to work, so they can't be switched off. We do not use analytics or marketing cookies.

Your Sites set their own cookies, which you control and must disclose to your visitors.

7. How long we keep data

Data How long
Account, order and subscription records While your account is open, then as long as tax and accounting law requires. Financial records are kept for 7 years.
API and dashboard request logs 30 days
Our own database backups (encrypted) One per day for 14 days and one per week for 8 weeks

We use encryption in transit (HTTPS), encrypt our database backups before they leave the server, keep each Site in its own containers with its own database and password, and limit who can access production systems. Depending on where you live, you may have the right to:

EU and UK (GDPR). Our legal bases are listed in section 3: contract, legitimate interests, legal obligation and consent.

AnyPress is for businesses and people aged 18 and over. We don't knowingly collect data from children. Customers whose Sites are aimed at children are responsible for following the laws that apply to them, such as COPPA.

  • Third-party costs you paid to others, such as domain registration, premium plugins or your own payment provider's fees.

Chargebacks

Please contact us before disputing a charge with your bank; we can usually sort it out faster. If you file a chargeback, the plan it relates to may be suspended while the dispute is open. Only the Site on the disputed plan is affected; your other Sites keep running.

Where the law gives you more

Nothing in this policy limits any refund rights you have under the consumer protection laws that apply to you.

Contact

support@anypress.io

CHANGES.title: 13 ready-made pages, with forms that ask one question at a time
CHANGES.body: Add a quote request, project inquiry, client onboarding, home valuation, pickup order, visit planner, consultation booking and more from your page library. Each comes fully designed in your site's look, with real photos and text you can change. Their forms show one question at a time, like a short survey, so visitors finish them instead of facing one long form.

CHANGES.title: Ninja Tables without the Pro upsells
CHANGES.body: The tables screens in your dashboard no longer show upgrade badges, locked Pro options, review requests or ads for other plugins. You see only the tools you can use.

CHANGES.title: Making a demo your site keeps only your own work
CHANGES.body: When you turn a demo you changed on /try into your site, the demo's sample tables, charts, booking pages and sample forms stay behind, and the sections that only introduced them go too. Everything you wrote, your photos and your contact and newsletter forms come with you.

CHANGES.title: Tables and charts on any page
CHANGES.body: Sites now come with Ninja Tables and Ninja Charts. Put a price list, size guide, timetable or menu on any page, and visitors can sort and search it. Turn a table into a bar, line or pie chart, and the chart updates when you change the table.

link.label: See it on a demo site

CHANGES.title: Events for your community
CHANGES.body: Community sites now come with FluentEvent. Post an online or in-person event in any space, members say they're going from the event card, and you check people in on the day. Public classes and meetups get their own page that anyone can sign up from, with reminder emails sent for you.

CHANGES.title: Try a bookings site set up for a law office
CHANGES.body: A new demo shows a Bookings Site made for a law office: one consultation form asks what the client needs, shows only the questions for that, and books them with the right lawyer. It also has the firm's flat fees table, client help desk and six months of posts. Open it from the Bookings Site page.

CHANGES.title: Demos say they aren't saved
CHANGES.body: Trying a site on the Try page now says plainly that the demo runs in your browser and is cleared when you close the tab, and your browser asks before you close it. Make This My Site keeps your changes.

CHANGES.title: Aisle: a finished design for clothing shops
CHANGES.body: A home page that opens on a full-screen photo, your categories as photos edge to edge, a lookbook, gift cards and a help centre that's already written: shipping, returns and exchanges, a size guide and track an order.

CHANGES.title: Care without a call first
CHANGES.body: Want us to make changes to your site? Pick a care package straight after checkout or from your account, no call to book first.

CHANGES.title: Move in from Calendly, Skool, Brevo and MailerLite
CHANGES.body: Booking sites can bring their Calendly hours, event types and upcoming bookings. Communities can bring their Skool members. Any site can bring its Brevo or MailerLite contacts into FluentCRM.

CHANGES.title: A cancellation form for shoppers in Europe
CHANGES.body: Every site that sells with FluentCart now has the 14-day cancellation form EU and UK shoppers have a right to, with each request kept on its order.

CHANGES.title: New arrivals and categories on your shop's home page
CHANGES.body: Your shop's home page shows your newest products and a Shop by category row, so shoppers see what you sell straight away.

CHANGES.title: Seven days free, on every plan
CHANGES.body: Start any site and try it for 7 days before you pay. Add a card when you start, and cancel before day 8 to pay nothing. One free trial per person.

CHANGES.title: More room when you need it
CHANGES.body: Add 25 GB of storage to any site from your account. Packs stack, and you can pause or cancel one any time.

CHANGES.title: Your community on your home page
CHANGES.body: Show your community on your home page from Settings, Reading, so members land in their feed. Members stay out of wp-admin and only ever see your community.

CHANGES.title: Courses and members from Tutor LMS, LifterLMS and MemberPress
CHANGES.body: Bring your courses with their lessons and students' progress from Tutor LMS or LifterLMS, and your active MemberPress members into their spaces and courses.

CHANGES.title: Download a copy of your whole site
CHANGES.body: Tools, Download my site gives you one zip of your whole site, files and database included, that restores on any WordPress host. Your site is yours.

CHANGES.title: Shop pages that match your design
CHANGES.body: FluentCart's product, cart and checkout pages now follow your site's colours and fonts.

CHANGES.title: Your site in more than one language
CHANGES.body: Turn on the Languages switch and Polylang is set up for you, with a language switcher in your menu.

CHANGES.title: A cleaner wp-admin
CHANGES.body: Your WordPress Dashboard opens on a tidy home page with what you need, without other plugins' notices and upsells.

BLOCKS.title: Popup
BLOCKS.body: A box over the page after a few seconds, on scroll or when someone is about to leave. Good for a signup or an offer.

BLOCKS.title: Carousel
BLOCKS.body: Slides that scroll sideways with arrows and dots, for reviews, projects, team members or photos.

BLOCKS.title: Before and after
BLOCKS.body: Two photos of the same job with a handle to drag between them: a kitchen, a lawn, a haircut, a roof.

BLOCKS.title: Countdown
BLOCKS.body: Days, hours and minutes left until an offer ends or an event starts.

BLOCKS.title: Counter
BLOCKS.body: A big number that counts up as it comes into view, such as years in business or jobs done.

BLOCKS.title: Star rating
BLOCKS.body: Your rating, how many reviews and where they're from, for example 4.9 out of 5 on Google.

BLOCKS.title: Map
BLOCKS.body: Your address on a map with a pin and a link for directions.

BLOCKS.title: Location finder
BLOCKS.body: All your branches next to a map. Visitors search by town or tap “Near me” to find the closest.

BLOCKS.title: Notice bar
BLOCKS.body: One short line across the page, such as holiday hours or free delivery. Visitors can close it.

BLOCKS.title: Call and book bar
BLOCKS.body: A bar along the bottom of the screen with Call and Book buttons, so the main action is one tap away.

BLOCKS.title: Age check
BLOCKS.body: Asks visitors to confirm their age before they see the site, for shops selling age-restricted goods.
